title: Non-Relational Database
subtitle: Blob, Data Lake, Files, Tables and Cosmos DB without the jargon.

what.body: Non-relational (NoSQL) storage drops rigid tables for flexible models that scale out worldwide: documents, key-values, graphs, files and objects. Choose it when shape varies, volume explodes, or users are everywhere.
what.example: A chat app stores each message as JSON (fields differ per message type), photos in Blob Storage, and serves both from the nearest region with Cosmos DB.

concepts.body: Flexible schemas + horizontal scale-out + tunable consistency. Built for huge, varied, distributed data.
Self-contained JSON-like records. A customer document can nest addresses and order arrays inside itself.
Every item = unique key + value. Fastest lookups when you always fetch by key: sessions, carts, settings.
Nodes plus edges. Friends, fraud rings, recommendations — anything where relationships ARE the data.
Add more servers instead of a bigger one. How NoSQL absorbs viral growth.
The field Azure uses to spread data and traffic across partitions. Pick something high-cardinality like UserID — never a field with 3 values.
Cosmos DB's throughput currency: how many reads/writes per second you provision. Bigger queries cost more RUs.
How fresh reads must be: Strong (strictest) → Bounded Staleness → Session (the default) → Consistent Prefix → Eventual (fastest).
TTL auto-deletes old items (sessions, carts). Change feed streams every insert/update to Functions or analytics.

examples.title: One chat message as a document
examples.body: Text, image and poll messages share one store — each carries only its own fields.

examples.title: Table Storage addressing
examples.body: PartitionKey groups, RowKey identifies. Fastest reads use both.

examples.title: Blob tiers at a glance
examples.body: Match tier to how often you read: Hot (daily) → Cool (monthly) → Archive (almost never, rehydrate first).

services.name: Azure Blob Storage
services.when: You have files or archives, not rows.
services.scenario: Millions of product photos with Hot/Cool/Archive tiers.

services.name: Data Lake Storage Gen2
services.what: Blob Storage plus a folder hierarchy.
services.when: Spark/Hadoop analytics over lakes of files.
services.scenario: Training models on years of clickstream logs.

services.name: Azure Files
services.scenario: Retiring the office file server without rewrites.

services.name: Azure Table Storage
services.when: Billions of small lookups, tiny budget.
services.scenario: Device readings keyed by sensor + timestamp.

services.name: Azure Cosmos DB
services.scenario: Game leaderboards and carts on every continent.

remember: Flexible schema + scale-out = NoSQL. Fixed schema + scale-up = relational.
Hot = often · Cool = monthly · Archive = almost never (rehydrate first).
Table Storage = PartitionKey + RowKey, cheapest. Cosmos Table API = same model, global + SLA.
Cosmos APIs: SQL→JSON queries · Mongo→migration · Cassandra→telemetry · Gremlin→relationships · Table→key-value.
API is fixed at account creation · Session is default consistency · Throughput = RU/s · TTL expires old items.

quickCheck.q: Video archive, rarely watched. Where + which tier?
quickCheck.a: Blob Storage, Archive tier (rehydrate before reading).

quickCheck.q: Migrating a MongoDB app with minimal changes?

quickCheck.a: Gremlin (graph) API — relationships are the query.
